nphi.title: Strengthening Biosecurity in Southeast and Eastern Europe (Biosecurity SEEE)
nphi.with: Georgian NCDC; Bundeswehr Institute of Microbiology; GIZ; BACAC; WHO; US DTRA; ISTC; STCU
nphi.summary: RIVM coordinated needs-based biosafety and biosecurity capacity building, including national assessments, pathogen inventories and train-the-trainer courses in Georgia.

nphi.title: EU CBRN CoE P53 – Strengthening biosafety and biosecurity in Central Asia
nphi.with: ISTC (Kazakhstan); VERTIC; Public Health England; Sustainable Criminal Justice Solutions (lead)
nphi.summary: RIVM led the biosecurity training and supported the biosafety training, including hands-on BSL3 work, for national expert teams in seven countries.

nphi.title: STEP – immunisation policy capacity
nphi.summary: Building technical capacity for evidence-based decisions on immunisation policies in 16 countries of the WHO European Region.

nphi.title: TÜSEB – Kazakhstan National Research Center for Health Development MoU
nphi.with: Salidat Kairbekova National Research Center for Health Development
nphi.summary: MoU signed in Ankara in 2025 for cooperation on health research, biotechnology, drug development, healthcare quality and accreditation, telemedicine and workforce capacity building.

nphi.title: Kazakhstan–Kyrgyzstan MoU on biological security in Central Asia
nphi.actor: National Scientific Center of Especially Dangerous Infections (Kazakhstan)
nphi.with: Republican Center for Prevention of Especially Dangerous Infections (Kyrgyzstan)
nphi.summary: A 2024 MoU between the two countries' especially-dangerous-infection centres on joint biosafety research, monitoring and information exchange on dangerous infections, and specialist training.

nphi.title: CDC Eastern Europe and Central Asia Regional Office (EECA)
nphi.with: Ministry of health counterparts (not named); regional FETP
nphi.summary: CDC's EECA regional office in Tbilisi (2021) supports ten countries on AMR, hepatitis C elimination, genomic sequencing, lab quality, surveillance, workforce development and pandemic preparedness.

nphi.title: China–Kazakhstan exchange on plague and zoonotic disease control
nphi.with: National Scientific Center for Especially Dangerous Infections (NSCEDI), Kazakhstan
nphi.summary: Kazakhstan's NSCEDI delegation visited China CDC and Xinjiang in 2023 to exchange on surveillance of plague, anthrax, tularemia and brucellosis. The visit built on Belt and Road plague meetings held since 2018.

nphi.title: CDC Central Asia regional office (Almaty)
nphi.with: Ministries of health; National Center for Public Health of Kazakhstan (Scientific Practical Center for Sanitary Epidemiological Expertise and Monitoring); National Center for Antimicrobial Resistance (Uzbekistan); Central Asia FETP; GLLP
nphi.summary: CDC established a Global Disease Detection office in Kazakhstan in 1995 and supports Central Asian MOHs and Kazakhstan's National Center for Public Health with FETP, lab training, AMR, One Health (CCHF), HIV and hepatitis.

nphi.title: Seminar on Plague Prevention and Control in SCO Countries
nphi.with: Plague and public health experts from SCO member and observer states; Wu Lien-Teh Foundation
nphi.summary: A 2025 Beijing seminar, followed by a Xinjiang–Central Asia technical exchange, to advance technical collaboration and joint plague control mechanisms among SCO countries.

nphi.title: EMIS-2023 – European MSM internet survey extended to Eastern Europe/Central Asia
nphi.with: Deutsche Aidshilfe (Germany); ECOM – Eurasian Coalition on Health, Rights, Gender and Sexual Diversity; SEE RCN – South Eastern Europe Regional TB and HIV Community Network
nphi.summary: Extended online health and behaviour surveys among MSM to EECA and Western Balkans to strengthen HIV/STI surveillance.

nphi.title: BoCO-19 – Corona Global – Burden of COVID-19 population health metrics
nphi.with: National Association of Public Health (Albania); Public Health and Reforms Center (Azerbaijan); IPH FBiH & PHI Republika Srpska (Bosnia and Herzegovina); NCDC Georgia; Al-Farabi Kazakh National University; 'Healthy Future' (Kyrgyzstan); IPH Kosovo; Mongolian National University of Medical Sciences; IPH Montenegro; University of Belgrade (Serbia); Ministry of Health (Türkiye); Ukrainian Institute on Public Health Policy & Public Health Center (Ukraine); Tashkent Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education
nphi.summary: Harmonised burden-of-disease methods for COVID-19 and tested them for outbreak surveillance.

nphi.title: COVIMPACT Hepatitis – Corona Global – COVID-19 impact on hepatitis elimination in EECA
nphi.summary: Assessed pandemic impact on hepatitis B/C elimination programmes and supported recovery strategies.

nphi.title: Quadrilateral plague prevention and control cooperation (China–Russia–Mongolia–Kazakhstan)
nphi.with: Russian Research Anti-Plague Institute 'Microbe'; National Center for Zoonotic Disease (Mongolia); National Scientific Center for Especially Dangerous Infections (Kazakhstan)
nphi.summary: China CDC hosted a 2021 webinar with plague institutes from Russia, Mongolia and Kazakhstan to share plague control technologies and work toward a joint cross-border plague control mechanism.

nphi.title: EURO NITAGs – Strengthening NITAGs in middle-income WHO EURO countries
nphi.with: WHO Regional Office for Europe – VPI Programme
nphi.summary: Built capacity of immunization advisory groups for evidence-based recommendations.

nphi.title: Joint WHO Europe–IANPHI seminars on building NPHIs through mergers
nphi.with: Public Health Center of Ukraine; WHO Regional Office for Europe; merged NPHIs of Belgium, France, Norway, Sweden, UK
nphi.summary: WHO Europe and IANPHI held three seminars, in Kyiv (2017), Warsaw (2018) and Moldova (April 2019). Merged NPHIs from Belgium, France, Norway, Sweden and the UK shared their experience with countries setting up NPHIs: Ukraine, Moldova,…

nphi.title: Global Disease Detection (GDD) Regional Centers network
nphi.with: Host ministries of health / national public health institutes (not named on source page)
nphi.summary: CDC set up ten GDD Regional Centers between 2004 and 2013, working with host governments on outbreak detection and response, laboratory capacity, field epidemiology training and pandemic preparedness.
